node.statement: Since L_{Z_t}=L_{U_0}+tL_D and ||L_D||<=(1+epsilon_r)||D||, the preceding inverse bound and q<=1/4 give ||tL_{U_0}^{-1}L_D||<=(3/2)(9/8)(1/4)=27/64<1. Neumann inversion makes every L_{Z_t} invertible, so solving Z_t bold-dot R=J supplies a right inverse. Together with the defect estimate and (1+epsilon_r)q^2/4<=2*(q+epsilon_r*q+q^2), this is exactly Z_t in calUbar_{q+epsilon_r*q+q^2} by def-approximate-unitary-space.
